C0.quote: The expert votes for her favorite candidate.
C0.note: Studies a voting rule and committee design that aggregate experts' votes into a single choice.

C1.quote: selects a candidate whose quality is at most 𝜀 worse than the best one
C1.note: Main results are upper and lower bounds on committee size for a regret guarantee. A running-time corollary exists (Cor. 4.10) but is not a main result, so AL is not coded.

C2.2.quote: each expert returns a ranking of her top 𝑘 candidates
C2.2.note: Main model is top-k strict rankings, with k=1 being a single vote for the favourite. k-approval ballots appear only in Sec. 3.2, as a setting where no committee guarantees low regret.

C2.3.quote: An expert evaluates each candidate as the candidate’s quality less the distance
C2.3.note: Experts hold perceived qualities, i.e. evaluations of candidates.

C2.4.quote: each expert will vote for who she believes is the best candidate
C2.4.note: The vote is the top of the expert's own evaluation, stated without a justification. The ranking is defined directly by the arg max of perceived quality.

C3.1.quote: expert 𝑖 votes for candidate 𝑗 if and only if 𝑗 maximizes the perceived quality

C3.2.quote: each expert will vote for who she believes is the best candidate
C3.2.note: Sincere voting is stated in words in the introduction and built into the model.

C3.3.note: No reason is given for sincere voting.

C4.1.quote: 𝑗 maximizes the perceived quality 𝑞 𝑗 −𝑑 (𝑒𝑖 , 𝑐 𝑗 )
C4.1.note: Rankings are defined as induced by perceived quality, i.e. quality minus distance. Applicability is arguable because the paper uses 'utilitarian view', 'utility' and 'perceived quality' for voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: the regret of choosing candidate 𝑗 ∗ under quality vector 𝑞 is defined as
C5.1.note: Regret against the best true quality is an additive analogue of distortion. Coded Y with some doubt, since quality is a candidate property rather than voter welfare.

C5.2.quote: max 𝑗 𝑞 𝑗 − 𝑞 𝑗 ∗
C5.2.note: Regret is evaluated on true qualities, which are separate from the submitted rankings.

VOT.quote_behav: each expert will vote for who she believes is the best candidate
VOT.note: Experts vote according to their biased evaluation.

CAN.note: Candidates only have a location and a quality and take no action.

ORG.note: The planner's choices are coded under DES instead.

DES.quote_behav: We study how to select a committee of experts and aggregate
DES.quote_info: the planner cannot observe candidates’ qualities
DES.note: The planner chooses the committee and voting rule to guarantee regret at most ε. It sees the votes and the locations but not the qualities.

C7.1.quote: each expert will vote for who she believes is the best candidate
C7.1.note: DES is STRAT and VOT is NONSTRAT.

C7.2.note: No reason is given for modelling the two types differently.

C8.1.quote: design a voting rule that minimizes regret over all quality vectors
C8.1.note: Committee and rule design is an optimisation problem for the planner; there is no equilibrium concept.

claims.quote: the dean could choose a committee that is diverse in the sub-fields
we believe that our committees remain potentially feasible for small 𝑑

C9.1.note: Claims about real hiring committees and the feasibility of the constructed committees.

C9.2.quote: An expert evaluates each candidate as the candidate’s quality less the distance
C9.2.note: The claims depend on the bias model and on sincere voting, and both are stated.
